questions.text: Comparing source-backed registration requirements, what is the sole proprietorship advantage over an architecture corporation?

options.text: It avoids all BOA and PRC professional authorization.
It is an individual practice form registered with DTI while the architect still maintains BOA/PRC authority.
It allows non-architect investors to control professional decisions.
It creates a separate Board-registered corporation.

questions.rationale: RA 9266 IRR defines sole proprietorship as an individual Architect registered with DTI, BOA, and PRC. The safe comparison is practice-form registration, not venture capital or corporate-liability language.
questions.explanation: Reverses the advantage—while corporations do have higher registration costs, that is not why sole proprietors have lower costs; it is because of simpler procedures. Contradicts the structure—sole proprietors cannot easily attract venture capital; investors prefer corporate structures with growth potential. Confuses specialization with expansion—specialty knowledge is individual, not structural; sole proprietorships limit multi-discipline teams. Sole proprietorships have minimal startup costs and simpler registration procedures compared to corporations, though they lack the capacity to attract investment capital or easily expand operations. Sole proprietorships offer low startup costs because they skip corporate formation formalities, but this simplicity limits growth capacity.

questions.text: A sole proprietor architect hires support staff. What remains true under the source-backed RA 9266 framing?

options.text: The staff become the professional registrants for the practice.
The individual registered architect remains the professional authority for the architectural practice.
The office automatically becomes an architectural partnership.
DTI registration alone authorizes anyone in the office to practice architecture.

questions.rationale: Staffing does not change the RA 9266 rule that practice authority is tied to the registered/licensed architect and the required BOA/PRC authorization.

questions.text: Which statement is source-safe for a sole proprietorship under RA 9266 IRR?

options.text: It is a SEC-registered group of two or more Architects.
It is an individual Architect practicing and delivering architectural services with DTI, BOA, and PRC registration.
It is a corporation with a 75 percent RLA shareholder threshold.
It is a project-based joint venture between firms.

questions.rationale: The RA 9266 IRR definition expressly describes sole proprietorship as an individual Architect with DTI, BOA, and PRC registration.

questions.text: Before a sole proprietor may practice architecture or use the title Architect, what RA 9266 requirement must be satisfied?

options.text: Only a DTI trade name is required.
The person must have the required Board registration and Professional Identification Card.
A corporate board must approve the practice.
A foreign counterpart must sign the documents.

questions.rationale: RA 9266 Section 25 requires Board registration and a Professional Identification Card before practicing architecture or using the title Architect.

questions.rationale: DTI identifies the individual practice form, while RA 9266 Section 25 controls authority to practice architecture and use the title Architect.
